sources.title: Improved Fuel Cell Catalysts with Less Platinum
sources.support: The article explicitly describes platinum as rare and costly and its catalytic role in selected fuel cells. It supports the chosen example, not all batteries or all fuel-cell technologies.

sources.title: Types of Fuel Cells
sources.support: PEM cells use platinum or platinum-alloy catalysts and hydrogen/oxygen. This justifies the named electrochemical-source application. The generated block is not a literal electrode/membrane schematic.

sources.title: Platinum-group elements
sources.support: Platinum is among the platinum-group elements that tend to occur together in deposits; PGEs are mined in relatively few locations. Ore/mining and metal recovery are supported as an overview. Initial retrieval succeeded; repeated opens later timed out. No detailed mining mechanism is taken from the image.

sources.title: Bauxite and Alumina Statistics and Information
sources.support: Bauxite is an aluminium ore. Primary production generally refines bauxite to alumina and electrolytically reduces alumina. The pictured enclosed factory omits these intermediate stages rather than showing direct melting of bauxite.

sources.title: Nichteisenmetallindustrie
sources.support: UBA distinguishes primary ores from secondary scrap. It describes resource advantages and lower production energy for secondary aluminium while stressing that recycling always consumes energy. Sorting/refining matter. Mining and metal production use land, water and energy. These are qualitative factors, not a numerical life-cycle result.

sources.title: Batterien und Altbatterien
sources.support: Separate collection supports recovery of valuable materials and limits environmental release of harmful materials. Collected batteries are sorted and processed in professional recycling routes that recover material outputs. The image does not state a legal rule, universal chemistry or recovery yield.
